content: Balanitis refers to the inflammation and swelling of the foreskin and the glans (head) of the penis. Symptoms of Balanitis: Redness affecting the foreskin or the glans of the penis. The presence of other types of rashes on the penile glans. A foul-smelling discharge emanating from the affected area. Pain localized to the penis and foreskin. Causes of Balanitis: Balanitis is most commonly caused by inadequate hygiene practices in uncircumcised males. Additional potential causes include: Certain medical conditions, such as reactive arthritis or lichen sclerosus et atrophicus. Infections caused by bacteria, fungi, or viruses. The use of harsh soaps or failure to thoroughly rinse soap residue during bathing. Poorly controlled diabetes mellitus. Diagnosis: A healthcare provider can often diagnose balanitis based on a physical examination alone. However, in some cases, additional diagnostic tests may be required, such as: Skin tests to identify the presence of viruses, fungi, or bacteria. A skin biopsy, which may be necessary in certain situations to confirm the diagnosis. When to Seek Urgent Medical Care: It is important to inform your healthcare provider if you experience any symptoms of balanitis, such as swelling of the foreskin or pain in the affected area. Treatment Options: The treatment for balanitis depends on its underlying cause: If the condition is caused by a bacterial infection, antibiotics in the form of pills or topical creams may be prescribed. Balanitis associated with skin diseases may respond to the application of steroid creams. Antifungal creams are used when the condition is due to a fungal infection. In severe cases, circumcision may be recommended as the most effective treatment option. Circumcision may also be necessary if the foreskin cannot be retracted for proper cleaning. Prevention: Maintaining good hygiene is key to preventing most cases of balanitis. When bathing, it is essential to retract the foreskin to clean and thoroughly dry the area underneath. Prognosis: The majority of balanitis cases can be effectively managed with medicated creams and proper hygiene practices. Surgical intervention, such as circumcision, is typically not required.
